s: Who built famous Jama Masjid of Delhi ?

s: Creator of "Bibi Ka Maqbara/ Tomb of Bibi" was –
x: Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah (during Aurangzeb's reign) constructed "Bibi Ka Maqbara" for his mother Rabia-ud- Daurani which is an architectural wonder with intricate designs, carved motifs, imposing structures and beautifully landscaped Mughal style garden. It is known as 'Tomb of Bibi.” It is called ‘The Mini Taj’ or Deccan ‘Taj Mahal.’ It is also known as the tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani.

s: Who among the following has constructed a mausoleum for her emperor husband?
x: Haji Begum constructed a mausoleum for her husband Humayun at Delhi in 1565-1572 A.D. as ‘tomb of Humayun.’ Mirak Mirza Ghiyash, a Persian and his son Sayyid Muhammad, were the architect employed by Haji Begum for this tomb. It is the first double dome mausoleum of Mughal Architecture A garden, surrounds outwards of the tomb.

s: Who made the Red Fort in Delhi?
x: Shah Jahan transferred his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi) and laid the foundations of Shahjahanabad on his name. Red Fort is an important monument of Shah Jahan. It is an irregular octagon with two long sides on the west and east and with two main gates, one on the west and the other on the south called Lahori and Delhi gates respectively. It is unique in architecture and glory.

s: The finest monuments constructed by Akbar are found in–
x: A village named Sikri was located around 37 Km away from Agra, the famous SufiSage Shaikh Salim Chishti resided there. Akbar used to visit Sikri frequently for his blessings. The finest monuments constructed by Akbar is found in Fatehpur Sikri-Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Treasury, Panch Mahal, Khas Mahal, Kothi of Turki Sultana, Jodha Bai Mahal, Kothi of Mariyam, Birbal Ki Kothi, etc. are major complexes of Sikri. Percy Brown stated Sikri as "Pearl of Architecture" due to its elegance.

s: Who among the following deserves the credit for the construction of ‘Lal Qila’
x: Lal Qila (the Red Fort) at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan (1639-48) for his capital Shahjahanabad, not by Akbar, who built the Agra, Lahore and Allahabad forts.

s: Which of the following among Mughal Emperors constructed Jama Masjid of Delhi ?
x: Jama Masjid of Delhi was built up by Shah Jahan. He left behind a great legacy of structures constructed during his reign. Buildings constructed by Shah Jahan are Diwan-e- Aam, Diwan-e-Khas, Sheesh Mahal, Moti Masjid (Agra), Khas Mahal, Musamman Burj, Nagina Masjid, Jama Masjid (Delhi), Taj Mahal Red Fort etc.

s: Itmad-ud-Daula’s tomb at Agra was built by
x: Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula was built by Nur Jahan at Agra between 1622-1628 A.D. after the death of her father. This elegant monument is located on the left bank of river Yamuna. The main mausoleum is built with white marble. Itmad-ud-Daula has a special place in the chronicles of both history as well as architecture. The monument is priceless because this is the first tomb in India that is entirely made up of white marble. In spite of marble and inlay work, it was for the first time when a new style of ornamentation, Pietradura, was used.

s: Moti Masjid in the Red Fort at Delhi was built by :
x: Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort at Delhi was built by Aurangzeb. Mughal Administration *During the Mughal administration, the district was known as the ‘Sarkar’. Each Suba (province) was divided into several Sarkars (districts) for the convenience of governance. Sarkar was further divided into ‘Pargana’ or ‘Mahal’. The leading officers of each Sarkar were - Faujdar, Amalgujar, Qazi, Kotwal, Bitikchi and Khajandar. *Mir Bakhshi was the head of the military department during the reign of Mughals. He also fixed the monthly salary of soldiers by issuing a signed certificate called ‘Sarkhat’. Apart from this, there were Bakhshi's in the provinces who worked under the control of Mir Bakhshi. *In the Mughal regime, head of military department was called the Mir Bakshi and head of land revenue administration was Diwan/Wazir, and Mir Bakshi was responsible for the salary of the military department. *Sir Jadunath Sarkar stated Mir Bakshi as Vetanadhikari (Pay Master). The duty of the Pay Master was of Diwaan-i- Tan. During the Mughal period, in addition to the soldiers of Mansabdars, there were others two different types of cavalry who were called ‘Ahadi’ and 'Dakhili'. 'Ahadi's have been called gentlemen-troopers, being recruited directly by emperor and having their own muster-master. *‘Dakhili’ soldiers were also recruited by the Emperor although they were kept in the service of Mansabdars. *The prostitutes were expelled from the city and settled at some other place named ‘Shaitanpur

s: Jahangir Mahal is located at –
x: Agra Fort is the earliest example of Akbari style. This fort was built by Akbar. This monument was erected under the guidance of the chief architect of Akbar, Kasim Khan. Akbar had built more than 500 buildings in the fort by red sandstone. Jahangir Mahal is located inside of the Agra Fort. This palace was constructed for Shahzada Salim by Akbar. Jahangir Palace is one of the top examples of Mughal architecture with intricate Hindu and Islamic motifs. The architecture of Jahangir palace is inspired by the Palace of Man Singh of Gwalior.

s: Which one of the following buildings is known as 'Shani-Fatehpur'?
x: Mughal emperor Akbar established Fatehpur Sikri (City of Victory) city. Established in present day Uttar Pradesh, it was capital of Mughal Kingdom from 1571 AD to 1585 AD. It houses monuments of Mughal architecture of likes of – Jama Masjid, Buland Darwaja, Panch Mahal, Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti etc. Jama Masjid situated here is also known as 'Shah-i-Fatehpur' or 'Shan-i-Sikri'.

s: Where was Darashikoh buried?
x: Dara Shikoh was handed over to Aurangzeb by a Baluchi chieftain named Malik Jeevan. A special Judicial Committee appointed by Aurangzeb declared Dara a heretic and ordered the death penalty for him. Dara was killed in 1659 AD, his head was buried in Taj Mahal complex in Agra and the body was buried in Tomb of Humayun (Delhi). However many history books do not mention this.
